Compressed, base64-encoded JSON

Source: R/json_gzip.R
rmbl_json_gzip.Rd

json_gzip_encode() serialises to JSON, compresses with gzip and encodes the result as base64, so it can be embedded in another JSON document, a header, or a text column. json_gzip_decode() reverses all three steps.

Usage

json_gzip_encode(x, raw = FALSE, ...)

json_gzip_decode(txt, raw = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

Object to encode.

raw

Logical scalar, default FALSE: return (or, for the decoder, insist on) gzip bytes instead of base64 text.

...

For json_gzip_encode(), passed to bricklayer_json_to_json() (for example auto_unbox or digits); for json_gzip_decode(), passed to bricklayer_json_from_json() (for example simplifyVector).

txt

Base64 string (or raw vector of gzip bytes) from json_gzip_encode().

Value

json_gzip_encode() a length-1 character vector, or a raw vector when raw = TRUE. json_gzip_decode() the decoded object, as bricklayer_json_from_json() returns it.

Details

JSON is highly compressible because every record repeats the key names, so this is usually a large saving on anything record-shaped – but it is opaque. Use it for payloads that travel, and plain bricklayer_json_to_json() for anything a person is meant to read or a git diff is meant to show.

raw = TRUE skips the base64 step and returns the gzip bytes, which is what to use when writing to a file rather than embedding in text.

The bytes are a real gzip member (RFC 1952, with header bytes 1f 8b), readable by gzip -d, zcat and any HTTP client, not the zlib stream that memCompress(type = "gzip") returns. The modification time in the header is zero, so the same input always gives the same bytes and a digest of the result does not depend on the clock. The base64 text uses the standard alphabet with line breaks every 72 characters (bricklayer_json_base64_enc()).

The decoder takes the input's own type: a raw vector is read as gzip bytes whatever raw says, and text as base64. As a guard against decompression bombs it refuses a member whose declared uncompressed size is over 64 MiB. Errors: text given with raw = TRUE; text that is not base64; bytes that are not a gzip member (under 18 bytes or not starting 1f 8b); a declared size over 64 MiB; a corrupt member; invalid JSON inside.

Note that the JSON keeps data, not R types: a factor comes back as text and attributes are lost. Compress bricklayer_json_serialize() output when the object must come back exactly.

See also

bricklayer_json_to_json(), bricklayer_json_serialize() for an uncompressed form that keeps types and attributes.

Examples

x <- list(rows = data.frame(id = 1:50, value = stats::runif(50)))

enc <- json_gzip_encode(x)
substring(enc, 1, 40)
#> [1] "H4sIAAAAAAAA/1XTS0rFQBAF0L1k/JD6dH06WxEH"

# Smaller than the JSON it came from, because the keys repeat.
c(json = nchar(bricklayer_json_to_json(x)), gzip_b64 = nchar(enc))
#>     json gzip_b64 
#>     1245      433 

# Round trips.
identical(json_gzip_decode(enc)$rows$id, 1:50)
#> [1] TRUE

# Raw gzip bytes, for writing to a file.
bytes <- json_gzip_encode(x, raw = TRUE)
class(bytes)
#> [1] "raw"
identical(json_gzip_decode(bytes, raw = TRUE)$rows$id, 1:50)
#> [1] TRUE

# the bytes are ordinary gzip: a file any gzip tool can read
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json.gz")
writeBin(bytes, f)
substr(readLines(gzfile(f), warn = FALSE), 1, 40)
#> [1] "{\"rows\":[{\"id\":1,\"value\":0.333},{\"id\":2,"

# options pass through to the JSON writer and reader
json_gzip_decode(json_gzip_encode(list(a = 1, b = "x"), auto_unbox = TRUE),
                 simplifyVector = FALSE)
#> $a
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $b
#> [1] "x"
#> 

# text that is not a gzip member is refused
try(json_gzip_decode(bricklayer_json_base64_enc("not gzip")))
#> Error : `txt` does not hold a gzip member: expected at least 18 bytes starting 1f 8b, got 8 byte(s).
